headline: HYCROFT DRILLS BEST HOLE EVER — 30.5 G/T AU AND 1,727 G/T AG OVER 19.6M AT VORTEX ZONE, NEVADA
snippet: Hycroft Mining (Nasdaq: HYMC) reset its own record on October 13 with hole H26D-6175A at the Vortex zone in Nevada: 19.6 metres at 30.49 g/t gold and 1,726.72 g/t silver, including a 1.7-metre inner interval at 347 g/t gold and 9,526 g/t silver with visible gold present. CEO Ann Vlcek said the silver-equivalent grade is more than 50% above the company's previous best hole, and follow-up drilling is already underway at both the Vortex and Brimstone systems — the second consecutive year Hycroft has beaten its own record while advancing the project toward an updated resource estimate.

headline: COPPER RISES TO TWO-WEEK HIGH AS CODELCO HALT BITES — SILVER SLIPS BELOW $61 AHEAD OF US CPI
snippet: LME copper climbed to a two-week high on October 13 as Codelco's ongoing suspension of the El Teniente Andes Norte section — which has reduced one of Chile's flagship mines by roughly 27% year-on-year — tightened supply alongside the Centinela labour action already underway. Silver fell back below $61 per ounce as the US dollar held near 18-month highs ahead of Thursday's US Consumer Price Index release, which markets expect will determine whether the Federal Reserve signals a further rate increase at its October 27–28 meeting — a macro overhang that has suppressed silver's industrial premium relative to gold.

headline: URANIUM WEEK: EQUITIES RETREAT BUT SUPPLY THESIS UNCHANGED — KAZATOMPROM ACID WOES LOCK IN 2027 TIGHTNESS
snippet: FNArena's October 13 uranium weekly notes that listed uranium equities declined through the week despite an unchanged fundamental supply thesis, with spot U₃O₈ holding near $90 per pound and long-term contract prices above $96.50 per pound. The report highlights the Kazatomprom TQZ sulfuric acid plant — now delayed to 2027–2028 — as the core factor ensuring that 2027 supply models remain tighter than current equity pricing implies, and frames the current share-price retreat as a classic mid-cycle disconnect between commodity fundamentals and listed equities that has preceded sharp reversals in prior uranium bull markets.

headline: GETTY COPPER EXPANDS BC PROGRAM TO 20,000M+ — 46M @ 1.47% CU SPARKS TWO-RIG PUSH AT GETTY SOUTH
snippet: Getty Copper (TSXV: GTC, OTCQB: GTCDF) has expanded its 2026 drill program at the Getty Project in British Columbia's Highland Valley District to more than 20,000 metres following results that included a 46-metre interval at 1.47% copper at Getty South — strong enough to justify adding a second rig at the target. The program began in April with a 10,000-metre spring plan; the expansion reflects growing confidence in the scale of the copper system after results outperformed expectations. The Highland Valley District hosts Teck's Highland Valley Copper Mine, one of Canada's largest, making district-scale copper discovery potential here strategically significant for consolidation.

headline: THE BIG PICTURE FOR GOLD AND SILVER 'COULD NOT BE MORE POSITIVE' — FXSTREET LAYS OUT STRUCTURAL BULL CASE
snippet: An FXStreet analysis published October 12 argues that gold and silver's structural bull case is the strongest it has been in years — with US real rates moderating, central bank accumulation running at record pace, AI-driven industrial silver demand growing, and the Federal Reserve's rate cycle approaching its terminal point. The piece frames October's correction from gold's January $5,589 peak as a classic mid-cycle pullback that has historically created the best entry points of a long bull market, and cites GDX and GDXJ miner ETFs breaking decisively higher in August 2026 — the kind of producer-level repricing that typically precedes a sustained move up in explorers.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER CLOSE FIRST WINNING WEEK IN SIX — CHINA PHYSICAL BUYING SURGES AS ETF INFLOWS RETURN
snippet: Gold and silver finally closed a winning week on October 13 after five consecutive down weeks, as China stepped up physical gold purchases during the correction and institutional investors returned billions to gold-backed ETFs — two demand signals analysts associate with durable bottoms rather than technical bounces. The recovery provides early evidence that the pullback from January's $5,589 gold peak may be finding support near the $4,157–$4,165 range, aligned with the 200-day moving average. For junior mining investors, a confirmed base in bullion is the necessary precursor to a sector re-rating, as exploration valuations have compressed more severely than spot prices during the correction.

headline: CHINESE LITHIUM TUMBLES TO 10-MONTH LOW — EU HYBRID CAR DEAL DEEPENS DEMAND FEARS AS CATL MINE STAYS IDLE
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate futures fell to a nearly 10-month low on October 12, pressured by a new EU-China trade arrangement that curtails Chinese hybrid car exports — dampening a key growth vector for EV battery demand — while CATL's Jianxiawo mine remains closed pending environmental approval and monthly Chinese output stays near record levels at 115,000 tonnes. Prices are approximately half their May 2026 peak, and the sustained oversupply environment is forcing a bifurcation between low-cost spodumene producers with locked-in offtake agreements and high-cost brine projects that require $20/lb or higher lithium to achieve project economics — exactly the kind of market that selects for quality junior developers.

headline: MINERS REVERSE MIDWEEK ROUT TO CLOSE GREEN — GDXJ +3.18%, GDX +2.95% AS SECTOR ROTATION BUILDS
snippet: SilverGoldAlpha's weekly ore report for the week ending October 13 documents how gold and silver mining ETFs reversed a sharp midweek selloff to close the week in positive territory: GDXJ rose 3.18% and GDX rose 2.95% on Friday, outperforming spot metals which ended the week lower. The report identifies an emerging divergence — miner ETFs gaining while gold ETFs finished roughly flat on Friday — as a potential early signal that institutional sector rotation is beginning ahead of anticipated year-end positioning. Junior gold stocks historically lead this type of ETF move on the upside by several sessions, making Friday's reversal a watch signal for TSX-V exploration names heading into Q4.

headline: MALAYSIA'S KING BUYS STAKE IN RARE EARTH MINER EXPANDING INTO JOHOR — S$6.1M INTO SOUTHERN ALLIANCE
snippet: Malaysia's Sultan Ibrahim — the country's current King — acquired a 2.25% stake in Singapore-listed Southern Alliance Mining for S$6.1 million on October 13. Southern Alliance is an iron ore miner actively expanding into rare earths, including a project in Johor where Sultan Ibrahim holds regional authority as Sultan. The move signals sovereign-level interest in capturing rare earth value domestically rather than exporting raw ore for Chinese processing, and aligns with Southeast Asia's accelerating push to develop rare earth beneficiation capacity ahead of China's November 10 deadline on heavy rare earth export controls.

headline: GRANDE PORTAGE COMPLETES 2026 DRILL SEASON AT NEW AMALGA GOLD, ALASKA — ASSAY RESULTS DUE Q4
snippet: Grande Portage Resources (TSXV: GPG) announced October 13 that its 2026 summer drill program at the New Amalga Gold Project in southeast Alaska is complete and the rig has been demobilized. The 2026 program — the company's largest in years — pivoted toward mine development planning rather than pure exploration, collecting systematic data to support a future feasibility study at the high-grade Juneau Gold Belt asset. Assay results from the summer program are expected in Q4 2026, making this a near-term catalyst; the announcement is largely logistical but confirms a fully-funded program was completed before the Alaskan winter closed access.
